# SQL Server (mssql) syntax matrix

<!-- generated by end2end/MssqlSyntaxMatrix - do not edit -->
Every case in [`cases/`](cases) is run through each sqlc build, the C# plugin, and SQL Server's own
`sp_describe_undeclared_parameters` / `sp_describe_first_result_set`, which act as the oracle for what
the parameter and result column types should be. See [README.md](README.md).

- **upstream**: sqlc main (3ad8b20)
- **patched**: sqlc main (3ad8b20) + scripts/sqlc-patches

| Legend | |
|---|---|
| ✅ | matches SQL Server |
| 🟡 | minor difference (sqlc is more conservative, or a compatible type of the same family) |
| 🟠 | wrong or missing type, nullability, name or column count |
| 🕳️ | the query is silently dropped from sqlc's output |
| ❌ | sqlc fails |
| 💥 | sqlc panics |

| | upstream | patched |
|---|---|---|
| ✅ Ok | 98 | 106 |

| 💥 Panic | 1 | 0 |
| **cases** | 187 | 187 |

C# plugin (on **patched** output): 157/158 generate, 157/158 compile.
